audit_findings.title: Owner-earnings anchor may omit required working-capital reinvestment
audit_findings.magnitude: $334.5 million 2025 working-capital outflow, equal to 47.7% of the $701.3 million anchor; deducting the full amount as a sensitivity reduces scenario values to approximately $35.84-$47.80 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Sustainable increases in receivables, inventory and other operating assets reduce OE and the cash available to support forecast growth.
audit_findings.evidence: Net cash provided by operating activities for the year ended December 31, 2025 of $634.1 million was primarily related to our net income of $701.4 million, adjusted for non-cash charges of $267.2 million and net cash outflows of $334.5 million from changes in our operating assets and liabilities.
audit_findings.explanation: The anchor demonstrably equals reported net income rather than cash-based owner earnings, while 2025 included a $334.5 million operating-asset-and-liability outflow. The sustainable portion is unresolved, so the full outflow is not automatically the correct deduction, but its scale is plainly capable of materially changing every scenario.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the OE reconciliation; normalize receivables, inventory, payables and other operating working capital over multiple years and seasonal periods; then rerun all scenarios using the sustainable incremental requirement.

audit_findings.title: The bridge may treat operating liquidity as excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: The $350.0 million revolver usage equals $2.44 per share; even excluding the entire $779.832 million cash balance would reduce value by only $5.43 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Required operating cash should be excluded from the excess-cash addition in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: During the year ended December 31, 2025, there were $350.0 million in draw downs on the 2023 Revolving Facility, which were all repaid during 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The revolver activity demonstrates seasonal funding needs but does not establish that $350.0 million, or any other amount, was permanently required cash. Nevertheless, the maximum possible correction is bounded by the full $779.832 million bridge addition. Removing all of it would leave scenario values at approximately $58.14-$81.01 per share, still far below the $173.38 market price, so this finding cannot change the valuation conclusion on its own.
audit_findings.action: Determine minimum operating cash from monthly balances, seasonal working-capital peaks, letters of credit and revolver usage; rerun the bridge only if the human owner wants a more precise intrinsic-value estimate.

audit_findings.title: Foreign cash may not be distributable at par
audit_findings.magnitude: At most the full $779.832 million cash addition, or $5.43 per share; the actual foreign-cash amount and repatriation friction are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Taxes, legal restrictions or other repatriation costs reduce the distributable portion of cash added in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025 and 2024, the cumulative undistributed earnings of the Company’s international subsidiaries remain indefinitely reinvested, and no liability has been recorded.
audit_findings.explanation: Indefinite reinvestment is demonstrated, but the record does not identify how much June 2026 cash belongs to foreign subsidiaries or the cost of accessing it. Because foreign cash is necessarily a subset of the $779.832 million total cash balance, even a 100% haircut to all cash would not alter the conclusion that the shares trade far above modeled value.
audit_findings.action: Obtain cash by legal entity and jurisdiction, identify withholding taxes and distribution restrictions, and replace face-value foreign cash with its net distributable amount if bridge precision is required.

audit_findings.title: Material control weaknesses affect the anchor and bridge accounts
audit_findings.mechanism: Misstatements in revenue, receivables, inventory, cost of sales or closing entries could change OE; balance-sheet misstatements could also change cash, debt or other bridge items.
audit_findings.evidence: Management has identified pervasive material weaknesses throughout the Company’s internal control processes that involve the control environment and control activities components of the COSO framework and additional material weaknesses in information technology general controls, the Company’s accounting for revenue and accounts receivable and inventory and cost of goods sold, and the financial statement close process.
audit_findings.explanation: The control deficiencies are demonstrated and remained unremediated at June 30, 2026, but no specific misstatement is demonstrated. The audited 2025 statements received an unqualified financial-statement opinion, management reported no material misstatement or restatement, and the June 2026 statements are unaudited. The weaknesses therefore create unresolved estimation risk, but this record cannot establish its valuation magnitude or direction.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the June 2026 balance sheet and OE source accounts; inspect subsequent filings, reserve true-ups, customer-incentive lookbacks and inventory adjustments; rerun only for identified corrections or revisions.

audit_findings.title: A volatile foreign-currency gain may remain in recurring OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $36.059 million pre-tax; approximately $28.1 million after applying the filed 22.1% ETR, equal to 4.0% of the anchor and approximately $2.33-$3.25 per share across the valuation scenarios
audit_findings.mechanism: Because the anchor equals GAAP net income, the transactional FX gain enters OE and is capitalized through the forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Foreign currency transaction (gains) losses were $( 36.1 ) million, $ 16.1 million and $ 5.0 million for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated normalization error unless the OE workpapers contain an undisclosed offset: 2025 net income included the $36.059 million gain, and the supplied valuation shows no removal. Its computed value effect is modest relative to both the $63.57-$86.44 scenario range and the $173.38 market price, so correcting it would not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Remove the 2025 transactional FX gain, substitute a documented normalized amount if appropriate, and rerun the scenarios to refine value per share.

audit_findings.title: The anchor includes an expressly one-time tax benefit unless normalized
audit_findings.magnitude: The 1.3-percentage-point ETR decrease applied to $900.278 million of pretax income equals approximately $11.7 million, or 1.7% of the anchor, corresponding to approximately $0.97-$1.35 per share across scenarios; the exact benefit is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A one-time reduction in tax expense increases net income and therefore the OE anchor that is capitalized in the DCF.
audit_findings.evidence: The decrease in the ETR from 2024 to 2025 is primarily related to one-time benefits recorded in the fourth quarter of 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The existence of a one-time benefit is demonstrated, although its exact amount is not separately filed. Using the complete 2024-to-2025 ETR decrease as a scale proxy produces only a small value effect relative to the modeled values and the gap to the $173.38 market price. It therefore is not reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion by itself.
audit_findings.action: Identify the fourth-quarter tax entries, remove the exact nonrecurring benefit, adopt a sustainable cash tax rate and rerun the scenarios for precision.
